claim_ceiling: Stage 11N may establish exact public-source identities, the annotated witness pattern, transcript anchor times, a later non-overlapping 30 fps null window, a contextual 60 fps clip spanning one transcript report, a threshold-defined ten-pixel lunar footprint in that transcoded clip, the absence of a screened pulse under the frozen rule, an approximate distance-based visibility advantage, a conservative all-lunar one-hour detected-count floor under explicit assumptions, the absence of a public calibrated exposure denominator, NASA's candidate-level description of a volunteer image, and a source-grounded measurement design. It cannot promote the pixel screen to source photometry or an event exclusion, promote the count floor to a completeness-corrected or brightness-threshold flux or an independently measured impact rate, establish a calibrated impactor-size distribution, assign exact one-to-one timing to all five annotated events, claim a simultaneous camera non-detection of any confirmed event, confirm a ground match to a crew event, independently prove the cause of every candidate, establish instrument flight readiness, claim NASA acceptance, or claim global novelty.

count_floor_assumptions: All five annotated events are accepted as impacts.
All five occurred within the nearly hour-long eclipse, conservatively rounded up to one hour.
The entire lunar surface is used as the maximum spatial denominator.
The value is not corrected for missed events, brightness threshold, detection completeness, or long-run sampling uncertainty.
geometry.interpretation: Approximate inverse-square point-source geometry only. It is not photometric calibration and does not establish flash luminosity, impactor size, or detection completeness.

ground_correlation_state: NASA publicly highlighted a volunteer impact-flash candidate but did not identify it as a confirmed match to a crew event; the crew record says the observed flashes were not expected to be Earth-correlatable.
most_consequential_archive_finding: The assessed 30 fps null video begins 15 minutes 13 seconds after the official five-event ledger timestamp, so it is a later null window rather than a simultaneous test of any confirmed event.

next_step_logic.if_a_public_calibrated_denominator_is_fo: Replace the no-rate conclusion with a brightness-thresholded effective area-time calculation and uncertainty analysis.
next_step_logic.if_a_source_identity_changes: Stop citation of the saved receipt, re-freeze the changed source, rerun the audit, and explain whether any conclusion changed.
next_step_logic.if_external_acceptance_is_needed: Provide the evidence receipt and exact sources to a lunar-impact specialist; do not relabel this local synthesis as independent scientific review.
next_step_logic.if_ground_candidates_are_found: Treat them as candidates until time, geometry, bandpass, and independent-detection criteria match a crew event.
next_step_logic.if_source_pixel_photometry_is_needed: Design a separate bounded packet-preserving extraction and calibration analysis; do not promote the transcoded contextual screen.
next_step_logic.if_sources_and_boundaries_verify: Use the receipt to strengthen the analysis around the exposure-denominator gap and the later-camera timing result.
next_step_logic.recheck_trigger: Any revised NASA report, newly released event-level timing or photometry, calibrated sensor data, ground correlation, or specialist review.

overlap_camera_finding: A separately materialized 60 fps SAW3 clip spans the 00:51:15.947 crew report, but the threshold-defined lunar image is only ten pixels across. A frozen screen found no qualifying pulse in the transcoded clip; that result is contextual and does not exclude the crew event.

recommendations.acceptance: Every crew event marker is either covered by calibrated frames or explicitly labeled uncovered with a reason.
recommendations.name: Continuous event-window coverage
recommendations.requirement: Run the dedicated impact sensor continuously across the complete dark-lunar observing interval, including pre-roll and post-roll, and publish verified live time.

recommendations.acceptance: The release records channel-level hits and the confirmation rule for every candidate.
recommendations.name: Independent optical confirmation
recommendations.requirement: Use two synchronized optical channels, separate detectors, or an equivalent independent discriminator so detector artifacts and spacecraft glints can be rejected.

recommendations.acceptance: Event, audio, camera, suit, PCD, and spacecraft times reconcile within a published maximum error.
recommendations.name: Spacecraft-clock event bookmarks
recommendations.requirement: Give each observer a voice or button event marker bound to the spacecraft master clock and a rolling pre-trigger and post-trigger buffer.

recommendations.acceptance: The release provides observer live time and the conditions needed to model human detection probability.
recommendations.name: Human exposure ledger
recommendations.requirement: Record observer, window, eyes-on-target intervals, target region, cabin illumination, dark-adaptation interruptions, and known reflections.

recommendations.acceptance: A versioned completeness surface accompanies any rate or flux claim.
recommendations.name: Injection-recovery completeness
recommendations.requirement: Inject synthetic flashes into representative flight backgrounds and publish recovery probability by brightness, duration, position, background, and channel.

recommendations.acceptance: A reader can trace every headline count to its evidence and see why excluded candidates were excluded.
recommendations.name: Candidate-level evidence receipt
recommendations.requirement: Publish confirmed, ambiguous, and rejected candidates with observer marks, coverage, detector results, timing uncertainty, location uncertainty, and final disposition.

recommendations.acceptance: Flux can be recomputed from candidate count and a machine-readable effective area-time curve.
recommendations.name: Effective area-time release
recommendations.requirement: Publish the brightness-dependent integral of detection probability over monitored lunar area and live time, not just duration or event count.

recommendations.acceptance: An end-to-end flightlike test recovers injected flashes across the disk and reports brightness and location errors at the required detection threshold.
recommendations.name: Target-scale sampling requirement
recommendations.requirement: Set the sensor field of view and angular sampling from predeclared localization and photometry objectives, then publish plate scale, point-spread behavior, and window effects across the lunar disk.
